what: First Android emulator session: the Flutter host played one real tapped game through the local stack and showed a live board update

device.emulator: Android Emulator AVD Pixel_6_API_34 (arm64-v8a), Android 14 (API 34), headless, SwiftShader GPU

app.build: flutter build apk --debug with --dart-define=MINIPLAY_URL=http://10.0.2.2:18080 and MINIPLAY_USER=droid1
app.gradle: 9.1.0 wrapper; the first build installed NDK 28.2.13676358 into the local Android SDK and took 237 s
app.cleartext: The merged debug manifest has usesCleartextTraffic=true (added by Flutter's Gradle plugin for debug builds only); the app's own manifests do not allow cleartext, so a release build still needs HTTPS.
app.cleartext_correction: Corrected 2026-10-23: usesCleartextTraffic=true came from the app's own main manifest, where it had been since M1; Flutter's Gradle plugin does not add it. Release builds therefore also allowed cleartext until 2026-10-23, when the attribute was replaced by a network security config that allows cleartext in debug builds only (see evidence/android_release_https_2026-10-24.json).

stack: Same disposable stack as the load profile: PostgreSQL 18.6 on 127.0.0.1:55432, Redis 7.4.11 and Kafka 3.9.1 containers, the six Go services, gateway on 127.0.0.1:18080 serving the freshly built web/dist; the emulator reaches the Mac's loopback as 10.0.2.2. A new per-run secret was used and not recorded.
steps_and_observations: Launched the host activity. The WebView loaded the gateway page over http://10.0.2.2:18080 and the host filled the player field with droid1.
Tapped Start, then tapped the pulse 16 times with adb input over the ten-second game (15 taps registered).
The page showed 'Finished rhythm: 100 points'; the Flutter host's bridge bar showed 'rhythm: 100 points · taps: 15', so start/progress/finish messages crossed the bridge and passed its parser.

SQL then held 1 attempt (accepted), 1 score (droid1, rhythm, 100, duration 10,009 ms), 1 outbox event (published), 1 processed event and a daily accepted count of 1. The REST all-time board listed droid1 with 100.

With the app idle, two players were scored from the Mac with cmd/load-probe (180 each). Without touching the emulator, its leaderboard updated to show both above droid1, so the WebView's live socket through the gateway delivered the frames.
Final SQL: 3 attempts, 3 scores, 3 outbox events all published, 3 processed events, daily accepted 3.
limits: One emulator session with taps injected by adb, not a person playing on a physical phone.
Debug build over cleartext HTTP to the host's loopback; no release build, HTTPS or real network.
Demo user ID supplied by the host; no authenticated identity.
